summary.text: Linda Lee represents the 23rd District on the New York City Council in eastern Queens, which includes Fresh Meadows, Bayside, Douglaston, Little Neck, Hollis and Queens Village.
Her Council biography says she was elected in November 2021 as the first Korean-American elected to the Council and the first woman to hold the seat.

paragraphs.text: Before taking office, Lee was President and CEO of Korean Community Services of Metropolitan New York, which her biography describes as the city's first community-based social service organization focused on the Korean community.
Earlier she worked in operations and administration at the New York State Health Foundation.
She holds a Master of Social Work from Columbia University and a bachelor's degree from Barnard College.
She served on Queens Community Board 11, as a Commissioner of the New York City Civic Engagement Commission, and on the board of the National Alliance on Mental Illness of New York City.
Lee lives in Oakland Gardens with her husband, Jie, and two sons.
